items.note: Tests an LLM-augmented divergent-thinking method for novice designers on the AUT and conceptual design tasks and reports higher fluency, flexibility, and originality; the abstract gives no comparison condition, assignment, or sample size, so the full text must confirm a no-AI or other-aid arm.

University of Oulu thesis in which 18 students did structured design exercises with traditional methods and with GenAI (ChatGPT, Midjourney), examining creative performance and design fixation; repository page returns 403, so details come from search snippets only, and the sample is far below 50.

Compares human-human teams with human-plus-AI teams (an AI 'Disruptive Interjector' that offers suggestions) on a design sketching task, with ideas rated by trained judges; the abstract does not say whether the AI is generative or how teams were assigned (data on GitHub).

Individual brainstorming experiment (n=52), human-only versus human with access to GPT-3.5 ideas, with flexibility (breadth of exploration) higher with AI ideas; assignment not stated and the data may overlap with Memmert and Bittner's later B&ISE paper.

System paper (Varif.ai, LLM plus text-to-image) with a controlled evaluation of 20 participants comparing it with baseline image-generation methods for reaching diverse image sets; the outcome is diversity of AI-generated images steered by users, and the sample is below 50; arXiv 2506.19644 is the same work.

Classroom quasi-experiment comparing an entrepreneurship course section encouraged to use generative AI for brainstorming startup ideas (n=53) with a section without AI (n=46); rubric scores were similar, and the sections were not randomly assigned (likely context_observational under codebook section 3).

Brainstorming on the D-Agree platform comparing humans alone, humans with GPT-3.5 IBIS agents, and agents alone, with two groups of three people; outcomes are counts of comments, ideas, and topics plus questionnaires, so the creativity measure is fluency only and the sample is tiny.

Solo-brainstorming system that shows a real-time uniqueness score computed against LLM-generated ideas, compared with a baseline condition on idea quantity, quality, and diversity (no significant effect); borderline scope because participants see a score rather than generated content (abstract from Semantic Scholar).

Randomized 2 x 2 field experiment with 371 professionals in South Korea (individuals vs teams, with vs without GenAI) on an open-ended innovation challenge; expert-evaluated innovation quality rose with GenAI.

Online experiment (N=200) in which participants wrote self-introductions with sentence completions from a model fine-tuned to favor interest, work, or hospitality topics; the outcome is the topics participants wrote about (convergence toward the AI's topic), which may fit across_people only if the task counts as creative writing.
